tours.title: Marian shrines
tours.sub: From Nazareth to the great places of pilgrimage to Our Lady

stops.name: Basilica of the Annunciation
stops.text: Built over the grotto venerated as the home of Mary, where the angel Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus. Every Marian pilgrimage begins with her yes.

stops.name: Basilica of the Holy House
stops.text: Home to the Santa Casa, revered since the Middle Ages as the house of the Holy Family. Our Lady of Loreto is the patroness of aviators.

stops.name: Jasna Góra Monastery
stops.text: The Pauline monastery that keeps the icon of the Black Madonna, Queen of Poland. Hundreds of thousands walk here every August.

stops.name: Knock Shrine
stops.text: Fifteen villagers saw Mary, Joseph and Saint John the Evangelist beside a Lamb on an altar at the gable of the parish church on a rainy evening in 1879.

stops.name: Sanctuary of Our Lady of Lourdes
stops.text: In 1858 Mary appeared eighteen times to Bernadette Soubirous at the grotto of Massabielle. Millions come each year, many of them sick, to pray and bathe in the spring.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of the Pillar
stops.text: Tradition holds that Mary appeared here on a pillar to the apostle James while he preached in Spain. Her feast on October 12 is a national holiday.

stops.name: Sanctuary of Fátima
stops.text: Where Mary appeared to three shepherd children, Lúcia, Francisco and Jacinta, in 1917, asking for prayer of the Rosary for peace.

stops.name: Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception
stops.text: The largest Catholic church in North America, dedicated to Mary under the title of the Immaculate Conception, patroness of the United States.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe
stops.text: Home of the tilma of Saint Juan Diego, on which the image of Our Lady appeared in 1531. It is the most visited Marian shrine in the world.

stops.name: National Shrine of Our Lady of Aparecida
stops.text: Fishermen pulled a small clay statue of Mary from the Paraíba River in 1717. Her basilica is among the largest churches in the world.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Luján
stops.text: Patroness of Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Young people walk the sixty kilometres from Buenos Aires to her basilica every October.

stops.name: Shrine of Our Lady of Kibeho
stops.text: Our Lady of Sorrows appeared to schoolgirls here in the 1980s, the first Marian apparitions in Africa approved by the Church.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health
stops.text: Known as the Lourdes of the East, it draws pilgrims of many faiths to the coast of Tamil Nadu, especially for its feast in early September.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of La Vang
stops.text: Mary is said to have comforted persecuted Catholics hiding in this forest in 1798. It is the national Marian shrine of Vietnam.

tours.title: Camino de Santiago
tours.sub: The French Way, from the Pyrenees to the tomb of Saint James

stops.name: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port
stops.text: Pilgrims gather their credentials here before climbing the Pyrenees. The Way begins at the Gate of Saint James.

stops.name: Royal Collegiate Church of Roncesvalles
stops.text: The first night in Spain after the mountain crossing. Pilgrims have received a blessing here at evening Mass since the Middle Ages.

stops.name: Pamplona Cathedral
stops.text: Santa María la Real, a Gothic cathedral behind a classical front, in the city of the running of the bulls.

stops.name: Puente la Reina
stops.text: Here the routes from across the Pyrenees join into one road and cross the Arga on an eleventh-century bridge built for pilgrims.

stops.name: Burgos Cathedral
stops.text: A masterpiece of Spanish Gothic and a World Heritage Site. El Cid lies buried beneath its great dome.

stops.name: León Cathedral
stops.text: The House of Light, with nearly 1,800 square metres of medieval stained glass.

stops.name: Astorga Cathedral
stops.text: Its cathedral stands beside the Episcopal Palace designed by Antoni Gaudí.

stops.name: Santa María la Real, O Cebreiro
stops.text: A pre-Romanesque church on the mountain pass into Galicia, remembered for a Eucharistic miracle in the fourteenth century.

stops.name: Church of San Nicolás, Portomarín
stops.text: A fortress church moved stone by stone up the hill when the old village was flooded by a reservoir in the 1960s.

stops.name: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral
stops.text: The tomb of the apostle James and the end of the Way. The great censer, the Botafumeiro, swings across the transept at special Masses.

tours.title: Great basilicas
tours.sub: The four papal basilicas of Rome and other great churches of the world

stops.name: Saint Peter's Basilica
stops.text: Built over the tomb of Saint Peter, the first pope. Michelangelo designed its dome, and the pope celebrates the great feasts of the year here.

stops.name: Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran
stops.text: The cathedral of Rome and the mother of all churches in the world. It is the pope's own cathedral as Bishop of Rome.

stops.name: Basilica of Saint Mary Major
stops.text: The oldest and greatest church in Rome dedicated to Mary, with mosaics from the fifth century. Pope Francis chose to be buried here.

stops.name: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
stops.text: Raised over the tomb of the apostle Paul on the road to Ostia, with a portrait of every pope in a band around the nave.

stops.name: Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi
stops.text: Two churches, one above the other, over the tomb of Saint Francis, with frescoes attributed to Giotto and Cimabue.

stops.name: Basilica of Saint Anthony
stops.text: Il Santo holds the tomb of Saint Anthony of Padua, Doctor of the Church and finder of lost things.

stops.name: Church of the Holy Sepulchre
stops.text: Encloses both Calvary and the empty tomb of Christ. Catholics share it with the Orthodox and other ancient churches.

stops.name: Basilica of the Nativity
stops.text: Over the cave where Jesus was born, entered through the low Door of Humility. Catholics worship in the adjoining church of Saint Catherine.

stops.name: Sagrada Família
stops.text: Antoni Gaudí's basilica of the Holy Family, under construction since 1882. Its central Tower of Jesus Christ made it the tallest church in the world.

stops.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Montmartre
stops.text: Its white domes crown the highest hill in Paris, and the Blessed Sacrament has been adored here day and night since 1885.

stops.name: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
stops.text: Modelled on Saint Peter's in Rome, it is among the largest churches in the world. Saint John Paul II consecrated it in 1990.

stops.name: Basilica of Bom Jesus
stops.text: Keeps the body of Saint Francis Xavier, the great Jesuit missionary to Asia. A World Heritage Site in Old Goa.

stops.name: Basilica of the Santo Niño
stops.text: Shelters the image of the Child Jesus that Magellan's expedition gave in 1521, the oldest Christian relic in the Philippines.

tours.title: Great cathedrals
tours.sub: Mother churches of the world's great cities

stops.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
stops.text: The Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité, reopened in December 2024 after the fire of 2019 was repaired.

stops.name: Chartres Cathedral
stops.text: Famed for its medieval stained glass and its labyrinth, and for the veil of the Virgin kept here since 876.

stops.name: Cologne Cathedral
stops.text: Its twin spires took more than six hundred years to finish. It holds the Shrine of the Three Kings, the relics of the Magi.

stops.name: Milan Cathedral
stops.text: The Duomo, crowned by 135 spires and more than three thousand statues, the largest church in Italy outside the Vatican.

stops.name: Florence Cathedral
stops.text: Santa Maria del Fiore, whose great dome by Filippo Brunelleschi is still the largest brick dome ever built.

stops.name: Seville Cathedral
stops.text: The largest Gothic cathedral in the world, with the Giralda bell tower and the tomb of Christopher Columbus.

stops.name: Toledo Cathedral
stops.text: The primate cathedral of Spain, with El Transparente, a baroque altar lit by a hole cut in the vault.

stops.name: Westminster Cathedral
stops.text: The mother church of Catholics in England and Wales, in striped red brick and stone, its walls glowing with mosaics.

stops.name: Saint Patrick's Cathedral
stops.text: The neo-Gothic cathedral on Fifth Avenue, opposite Rockefeller Center, and the seat of the Archbishop of New York.

stops.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City
stops.text: The largest cathedral in the Americas, built over two and a half centuries on the Zócalo, beside the ruins of the Aztec Templo Mayor.

stops.name: Cathedral of Brasília
stops.text: Oscar Niemeyer's crown of sixteen concrete columns. Four bronze evangelists stand guard at the entrance.

stops.name: Saint Mary's Cathedral
stops.text: Built of local sandstone, it is the mother church of Catholics in Australia, where World Youth Day was held in 2008.

stops.name: Manila Cathedral
stops.text: In Intramuros, the walled city. Rebuilt eight times after fires, earthquakes and war, it is the mother church of the Philippines.
